'''Willie Alford Thornton''' (born December 7, 1983) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[Club Atlético Peñarol (Mar del Plata)|Peñarol Mar del Plata]] of the [[Liga Nacional de Básquet]] (LNB). He had formerly played for the [[Los Angeles Clippers]], [[Washington Wizards]] and the [[Golden State Warriors]]. Collegiately, he played for [[Florida State University]].

==College career==
Thornton's outstanding four-year career at Florida State University was capped off by a stellar individual senior year that saw him make the AP [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] squad as a third team choice, a unanimous selection as first-team All-ACC, and was runner-up to [[Boston College]]'s [[Jared Dudley]] for the [[Atlantic Coast Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|ACC Player of the Year]]. He led the ACC in scoring and averaged over 7 rebounds per game as well. His season came to a disappointing end as the Seminoles did not qualify for the NCAA tournament for the ninth straight season and were forced to play in the NIT.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://seminoles.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/thornton_al00.html |title=Player Bio: Al Thornton :: Men's Basketball<!-- Bot generated title --> |access-date=2007-03-29 |archive-date=2007-04-01 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070401144107/http://seminoles.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/thornton_al00.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Los Angeles Clippers===
On June 28, 2007, Thornton was taken 14th overall in the [[2007 NBA draft]] by the [[Los Angeles Clippers]]. Thornton also has the same agent as Yao Ming.
On July 9, Thornton played his first summer league game for the Clippers, scoring 24 points and registering 8 rebounds, 1 assist, and 2 blocks in a 108–102 loss to the [[Denver Nuggets]].

In just his third preseason game as a rookie, Thornton led the Clippers to a win over the Golden State Warriors with 24 points on 11–15 shooting, including a perfect 2–2 from behind the 3-point arc while also connecting on all 8 of his first attempts from the floor.

With [[Ruben Patterson]] in the starting lineup at the start of the season, Thornton would not get the playing time he had received during preseason. Patterson was waived on December 13, 2007, in order to give the rookie more playing time.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.rotoworld.com/Content/playerpages/player_main.aspx?sport=nBa&id=557 |title=Ruben Patterson<!-- Bot generated title --> |access-date=2008-03-31 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080331171926/http://www.rotoworld.com/content/playerpages/player_main.aspx?sport=NBA&id=557 |archive-date=2008-03-31 |url-status=dead }}</ref> With a slew of injuries to the Clippers' big men, including [[Paul Davis (basketball)|Paul Davis]] with a torn [[Anterior cruciate ligament|ACL]], [[Tim Thomas (basketball)|Tim Thomas]] with recurring back and ankle injuries, and [[Elton Brand]] sidelined with a ruptured [[achilles tendon]], Thornton took advantage of his minutes playing [[Power forward (basketball)|power forward]] and [[small forward]] when teammate [[Corey Maggette]] was on the bench.

[[File:Al Thornton cropped.jpg|thumb|right|180 px|Thornton with the Clippers in March 2009.]]
On January 30, 2008, Thornton scored a then season-high 33 points against the [[Atlanta Hawks]], including a significant block in the final seconds in a 95–88 Clipper win.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20080203135229/http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=280130012 Reeling Hawks' comeback try falls short against Clippers]</ref> Thornton also recorded his first<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/3237/al-thornton Al Thornton: Complete 2007-08 Regular Season Game Log]</ref> [[Double (basketball)#Double-double|double-double]] on February 9, in a loss to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]], in which he had 18 points and 10 rebounds.<ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20120719123431/http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=280209020|title=76ers ride balanced attack to third straight win}}</ref>

On March 29, 2008, Thornton equaled a rookie franchise record (and Clippers season-high) 39 points on 13 of 23 field goal shooting, 3 of 6 from behind the arch, and 10 of 12 from the line in a 110–97 win over the [[Memphis Grizzlies]]. Thornton scored 20 of his 39 in the fourth quarter to seal the win and snap the Clippers' 10-game losing streak.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20080403014950/http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=280329012 Clippers stop Grizzlies to put end to 10-game drought]</ref>

On May 13, 2008, Al Thornton was named to the 2008 [[NBA All-Rookie First Team]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/news/all_rookie_080513.html |title=Durant, Horford Headline T-Mobile All-Rookie Team |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=2008-09-26 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080731112753/http://www.nba.com/news/all_rookie_080513.html |archive-date=2008-07-31 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On October 31, 2008, Thornton had a double-double with 30 points and 11 rebounds, a season high.

===Washington Wizards===
On February 17, 2010, Thornton was traded from the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] to the [[Washington Wizards]] as part of a three-team, six-player trade that sent [[Antawn Jamison]] from Washington to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]], [[Žydrūnas Ilgauskas]], a [[2010 NBA Draft|2010 first-round pick]] and the rights to [[Emir Preldžič]] from Cleveland to Washington, [[Drew Gooden (basketball)|Drew Gooden]] from Washington to Los Angeles, and [[Sebastian Telfair]] from Los Angeles to Cleveland.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/wizards/news/trade_100217.html|title=Wizards Acquire Ilgauskas, Thornton and First-Round Pick In Three-Team Deal|work=NBA.com|date=February 17, 2010|access-date=February 17, 2010| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20100219080600/http://www.nba.com/wizards/news/trade_100217.html| archive-date= 19 February 2010 <!--DASHBot-->| url-status=live}}</ref>

===Golden State Warriors===
On March 1, 2011, he reached a buyout agreement with the Wizards and was waived.<ref>{{cite news |last=Stein |first=Marc |title=Al Thornton bought out by Wizards |date=March 1, 2011 |work=ESPN.com |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=6172273 |access-date=March 1, 2011}}</ref> He signed a contract with the [[Golden State Warriors]] on March 3, 2011.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/thornton_signing_030311.html Warriors Sign Free Agent Forward Al Thornton] NBA.com, March 3, 2011</ref>

On March 14, 2011, Thornton scored 23 points against the [[Sacramento Kings]], his most points as a member of the Warriors.

===Puerto Rico===
On February 19, 2012, he signed with the [[Guayama Wizards]] of the Puerto Rican basketball league [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rotoworld.com/player/nba/1371/al-thornton.html|title=Thornton signs with Guayama Wizards|work=Rotoworld|date=February 19, 2012|access-date=February 27, 2012}}</ref> There he averaged 18.7 points per game.<ref name=CBA>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/world/asia/44219/al-thornton-signs-with-guangsha.html |title=Al Thornton signs with Guangsha |work=Sportando.net |date=September 29, 2012|access-date=September 29, 2012}}</ref>

===China===
On September 29, 2012, Thornton signed with the [[Zhejiang Lions]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]].<ref name=CBA/> Due to injury, he was replaced mid-season by [[Gary Forbes]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Pastuszek|first=Jon|title=Forbes for Thornton in Guangsha one of several mid-season import moves|url=http://www.niubball.com/2012/12/forbes-for-thornton-in-guangsha-one-of-several-mid-season-import-moves/|publisher=NiuBBall.com|access-date=14 December 2012|date=14 December 2012|archive-date=23 August 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170823021035/http://www.niubball.com/2012/12/forbes-for-thornton-in-guangsha-one-of-several-mid-season-import-moves/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Return to Puerto Rico===
In March 2014, he rejoined the [[Guayama Wizards]] of the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]].

===Japan===
On February 28, 2018, Thornton signed with the [[Shimane Susanoo Magic]] of the Japanese [[B.League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.susanoo-m.com/news/40659.|title=アル・ソーントン選手 契約締結のお知らせ|work=susanoo-m.com|date=February 28, 2018|access-date= 28 February 2018|language=ja}}</ref>

===The BIG 3===
Thornton had initially gone undrafted in the inaugural BIG 3 draft. Al was later acquired by [[Allen Iverson]]'s [[3's Company]] team.<ref>[[3's Company]]</ref>{{Circular reference|date=November 2017}} Al provided "3's Company" with scoring off the bench and went on to become the league's first [[4th Man]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/rashard-lewis-wins-first-ever-big3-mvp-stephen-jackson-named-best-trash-talker|title = Rashard Lewis wins first-ever BIG3 MVP; Stephen Jackson named Best Trash Talker| date=23 August 2017 }}</ref>

===Uruguay===
On August 7, 2020, Thornton signed with [[Club Atlético Aguada]] of the [[Liga Uruguaya de Basketball]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Al Thornton inked with Atletico Aguada |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/al-thornton-inked-with-atletico-aguada/ |website=Sportando |access-date=August 7, 2020 |date=August 7, 2020}}</ref>
